# Model Card — CedarLight Grid Models v0.1.0
*Synthetic data only. Seed 42. Generated by `run_ml.py`; numbers below are produced by that run.*

## 1. Intended use
Decision support for grid planners: (a) 24-hour-ahead feeder load forecasts, (b) 30-day asset failure-risk ranking to prioritise inspections. Outputs are **recommendations**; schedule proposals stay approval-gated. **Not** for real utility operations, switching, load shedding or customer-impacting decisions.

## 2. Data
Fictitious: 3 zones, 12 feeders, 60 transformers. 34,560 hourly feeder rows (2.2% readings missing); 2,160 monthly asset snapshots (failure base rate 9.2%). Zone C is deliberately older and has a higher true failure rate. The synthetic failure process drifts mildly upward over time (aging fleet).

## 3. Load forecaster — selected: `hgb` (chosen on validation MAE)
Features: hour (sin/cos), weekday, weekend, temperature signal, storm flag, 24h and 168h lags (lags only from data ≥24h old), feeder id. Time-ordered split (21,803/4,689/4,671); 4-fold `TimeSeriesSplit` CV on train.

| Model | Val MAE (kW) | Test MAE (kW) | Test MAPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| persistence_24h | 23.9 | 26.3 | 5.3% |
| seasonal_naive_168h | 23.3 | 18.8 | 3.7% |
| linear | 20.0 | 18.3 | 3.6% |
| hgb | 15.6 | 15.5 | 3.1% |

**Interval:** empirical 90% band from validation residuals (-6.9% / +5.5%). **Test coverage 87.2% vs 90% target** — slightly under-covered, so intervals should be treated as optimistic; widen or recalibrate before relying on them.

## 4. Failure-risk classifier — selected: `logreg` (highest validation PR-AUC; within 0.01 the simpler model wins)
Features: age, observed condition score, load ratio, heat hours, trailing-12-month faults. Time-ordered split by snapshot month (1440/360/360). Class imbalance (~9% positives) is handled by evaluating ranking metrics; models are **not** class-reweighted, because the agent consumes the predicted probabilities and reweighting would inflate them. Brier score checks probability quality.

| Model | Test AUC | Test PR-AUC | Brier |
|---|---|---|---|
| age_only_baseline | 0.773 | 0.637 | 0.875 |
| condition_only_baseline | 0.752 | 0.631 | 0.872 |
| logreg | 0.777 | 0.637 | 0.066 |
| hgb | 0.789 | 0.626 | 0.068 |
| mlp | 0.761 | 0.625 | 0.067 |

**Seed robustness (5 independent synthetic worlds, test split):**

| Model | AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|
| age_only_baseline | 0.798 ± 0.039 | 0.544 ± 0.120 |
| condition_only_baseline | 0.782 ± 0.030 | 0.527 ± 0.097 |
| logreg | 0.814 ± 0.031 | 0.564 ± 0.107 |
| hgb | 0.803 ± 0.030 | 0.524 ± 0.141 |
| mlp | 0.800 ± 0.042 | 0.511 ± 0.163 |

**Honest reading:** ranking quality (AUC / PR-AUC) of the learned models is close to the age-only and condition-only baselines, with differences inside seed-to-seed noise. A single test split has ~360 rows, so differences of a few AUC points should not be over-interpreted. The learned models' main practical benefit is **usable probabilities**: the baselines output raw scores, so their Brier values above are not comparable; among the probability models, lower Brier is better. The neural net did not beat logistic regression.

## 5. Fairness / coverage check (test split, flag top 10% of assets)
**Global ranking** — overall recall 0.53, recall gap between zones 0.80

| Zone | Failures | Recall | Share of zone flagged |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZoneA | 6 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| ZoneB | 9 | 0.00 | 0.01 |
| ZoneC | 30 | 0.80 | 0.29 |

**Zone-stratified quota** — overall recall 0.31, recall gap 0.29

| Zone | Failures | Recall | Share of zone flagged |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZoneA | 6 | 0.17 | 0.10 |
| ZoneB | 9 | 0.11 | 0.10 |
| ZoneC | 30 | 0.40 | 0.10 |

The global ranking is accurate but concentrates nearly all inspections in Zone C (it truly has the highest failure rate), leaving Zones A and B effectively uncovered. A per-zone quota narrows the gap at the cost of overall recall. **This trade-off is a policy decision for human operators;** the agent surfaces both options and does not choose silently.

## 6. Reinforcement-learning component (tabular Q-learning, toy inspection-selection MDP)
State (risk bucket, inspections left, blackout flag, position in the day); actions skip/inspect; reward = −inspection cost − failure cost. **Safety:** `inspect` is masked during blackout (storm) or when the crew budget is exhausted — in exploration *and* execution. Exact dynamic programming gives an optimum of about −6.58 reward per episode.

| Policy | Mean reward ± SE | Safety violations |
|---|---|---|
| random_legal | -9.17 ± 0.06 | 0 |
| never_inspect | -9.22 ± 0.07 | 0 |
| greedy_threshold | -6.56 ± 0.05 | 0 |
| q_learning | -6.53 ± 0.05 | 0 |

Q-learning matches the hand-written greedy threshold and the DP optimum within noise; it does **not** significantly improve on it in this small MDP. It is kept behind the `use_rl_policy` feature flag (default off). A first version that omitted the position in the day from the state performed no better than never inspecting — a Markov-state design error caught by comparison with DP.

## 7. Limitations and risks
- All data and ground-truth relationships are synthetic; real-world performance is unknown.
- Forecast ignores holidays and has no explicit seasonal drift model; intervals under-cover slightly.
- Small asset test set; ranking metrics are noisy. Parameters of the Bayesian network in `04_uncertainty/` are not yet fitted from this data.
- Models use no personal data; no customer-level information is modelled.
- Neural network: scikit-learn `MLPClassifier` (PyTorch was unavailable in this environment); it did not outperform logistic regression.

## 8. Governance
Artifacts are hash-recorded in `artifacts/metrics.json`. Model outputs enter the agent only as `Proposition`/`InferenceTrace` evidence and never upgrade an entailment status. Retrain and re-evaluate when data drift or coverage drops below thresholds in `configs/agent.yaml`.
